title: Graphical Exploration of the Vertical Shift Parameter D
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider f(x) = A\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{B}(x - C)\right) + D with A = 3, B = 6, and C = 0, so f(x) = 3\sin(\pi x / 3) + D. (a) Describe what happens to the graph on [-4\pi, 4\pi] as D increases through positive values D = 0, 1, 3. (b) What happens to the graph for negative values of D?
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Shifts vertically upward by } D \text{ units}; \quad \text{(b) shifts vertically downward by } |D| \text{ units}

steps.title: Identify the Role of D in the Sinusoid Formula
steps.explanation: The constant D is added outside the sine function, setting the horizontal midline y = D about which the wave oscillates with amplitude 3.
steps.why: Since -3 <= 3*sin(pi*x/3) <= 3, adding D shifts the range to [D - 3, D + 3].

steps.title: Part (a): Effect of Increasing Positive Values of D
steps.explanation: As D increases through positive values (0, 1, 3), the entire graph translates vertically upward by D units without altering its shape, period, or horizontal alignment.
steps.why: Adding a positive constant D to a function increases every y-coordinate by D.

steps.title: Part (b): Effect of Negative Values of D
steps.explanation: For negative values of D, the midline y = D lies below the x-axis and the entire graph shifts vertically downward by |D| units.
steps.why: Subtracting |D| from every output value translates the graph downward by |D| units.
